title: Transmission electron microscopic analysis of myelination in the murine central nervous system
protocol: Prepare the NE-1000 programmable single syringe pump.
Fill a 60 mL syringe with 20 mL of ice cold 0.9% saline and install it in the syringe pump.
Flush the system with 0.9% saline to remove air bubbles.
Adjust the pump flow rate to 1 mL/min.
Deeply anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneally injecting a mixture of ketamine (0.1 mg/g body weight) and xylazine (0.01 mg/g body weight) at 1.5 μL/g body weight.
Check the anesthesia by pinching the paw until there is no twitch response.
Stretch out the anesthetized mouse on a dissecting pan with needles, back down.
Wet the fur with 70% ethanol.
Use tweezers and operating/dissecting scissors to open the skin and expose the chest cavity.
Cut through the diaphragm to expose the heart.
Grab at the base of the sternum using tweezers.
Insert a 25-gauge winged infusion needle into the left ventricle without injuring the aorta.
Cut the right atrium immediately to prevent recirculation of the solution.
Perfuse with 0.9% saline until the liver becomes clear (approximately 20 min) at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Fill a new 60 mL syringe with 60 mL of 4% formaldehyde.
Take the infusion needle out of the mouse heart.
Remove the infusion tubing from the syringe containing 0.9% saline and remove the syringe from pump.
Install syringe with 4% formaldehyde in the pump, connect the infusion tubing to the syringe and remove air bubble.
Insert needle into left ventricle and perfuse for 60 min at a rate of 1 mL/min.
Exchange the flushing solution to 3% glutaraldehyde and perfuse for another 60 min at a rate of 1 mL/min.
Lay down the mouse with the back facing up on a dissecting pad.
Wet the fur with 70% ethanol.
Remove dorsal skin from head to tail.
Remove the muscle from the entire spine and expose the vertebrae using fine curved scissors with the blade tips facing up.
Decapitate the mouse head.
Gently hold the dorsal spine, insert straight supercut scissors laterally at the side of the spine canal and cut both sides of the spine.
Continue cutting along the entire spine until the whole spinal cord is exposed.
Gently lift the cervical spinal cord.
Cut the attached dorsal root ganglia on both sides.
Place the spinal cord on a Petri dish.
Cut the spinal cord into two pieces at the thoracic region.
Place the spinal cord in a 20 mL disposable scintillation vial containing approximately 15 mL of 3% glutaraldehyde for fixation overnight at 4°C.
Expose the skull by removing the skin.
Remove the connective tissue around the eyes to gain access to the eye socket.
Insert micro dissecting spring scissors carefully into the eye socket behind the eyeball.
Cut the optic nerve and remove the eye without stretching the nerves.
Cut the skull laterally on both sides using a scissor.
Cut the skull from the brainstem to the coronal suture along the sagittal suture.
Then cut the coronal suture.
Cut the skull along the lambdoid suture.
Remove the skull to expose the brain.
Insert forceps in a 45° angle into the forebrain and gently pull the brain out without stretching the optic nerve.
The optic nerves should stay attached to the brain.
Remove the optic nerve by cutting with micro dissecting spring scissors at the optic chiasm.
Pick up the optic nerves gently at the chiasm with forceps.
Transfer the optic nerves into the same scintillation vial containing 3% glutaraldehyde overnight at 4°C.
Place the brain into the same vial containing 3% glutaraldehyde for fixation overnight at 4°C in a refrigerator.
Dissect the optic nerve, spinal cord, or brain without bending or distorting the tissues after fixation.
Trim tissue slices using brain or spinal cord matrix to retain the region of interest.
Place the first blade in the channel at the true lambda.
Place three more blades in the anterior three consecutive channels.
Lift out the three slices between these two blades.
Transfer brain section #2 to a Petri dish for tissue trimming.
Store the other two sections in 3% glutaraldehyde.
Perform middle sagittal sectioning of the brain along the midline.
Divide the brain into left and right sides.
Remove the cortex by cutting along the dorsal side of the corpus callosum under stereo zoom microscope.
Cut the section again along the ventral side of the corpus callosum parallel to the dorsal cut.
Flip the corpus callosum to let the wider face lie on the Petri dish using ultrafine point forceps.
Cut a bevel at the outer edge of the corpus callosum as an embedding mark.
Transfer the corpus callosum in a new disposable scintillation vial containing 3% glutaraldehyde on ice.
Trim the corpus callosum by placing the blades close to the edge, keeping only the region of interest.
Remove tissue that is not of interest.
Slice brains from different mice at the same location to maintain consistency across different mice.
Separate the right and left optic nerves using a razor blade.
Transfer the separated optic nerves in the vial containing 3% glutaraldehyde on ice.
Place the spinal cord containing lumbar segments in the spinal cord matrix.
Insert the first blade in the lumbar enlargement.
Cut spinal cord into 1 mm sections by placing more blades in the anterior three consecutive channels.
Transfer the spinal cord slices in 3% glutaraldehyde on ice.
Fix optic nerves, corpus callosum and spinal cord slices from one mouse in a new disposable scintillation vial containing 15 mL of 3% glutaraldehyde at 4°C overnight.
Decant 3% glutaraldehyde, add cold 0.2 M sodium cacodylate buffer.
Wash tissues 2 × 10 min in a refrigerator at 4°C with 0.2 M sodium cacodylate buffer.
Place tissues for post-fixation in scintillation vials containing 2% osmium tetroxide for 1–1.5 h at RT in a chemical fume hood.
Wrap the vials using aluminum foil to protect the samples away from direct light.
Perform 2 × 10 min wash in cold 0.2 M sodium cacodylate buffer in a 4°C refrigerator.
Wash 2 × 5 min in cold distilled H2O.
Quick wash tissues with 50% ethanol and then perform 2 × 10 min wash in freshly prepared 50% ethanol at 4°C.
Quick wash tissues with 70% ethanol and then perform 2 × 10 min wash in freshly prepared 70% ethanol at 4°C.
Quick wash tissues with 90% ethanol and then perform 2 × 10 min wash in freshly prepared 90% ethanol at 4°C.
Quick wash tissues with 100% ethanol and then perform 3 × 20 min wash in 100% ethanol at RT (tissues acclimate to RT).
Quick wash tissues with propylene oxide and then perform 3 × 30 min wash in propylene oxide at RT.
Infiltrate tissues overnight in freshly made mixture of propylene oxide and embedding resin (1:1) at RT with rotation.
Agitate gently during tissue infiltration to prevent samples from attaching to the vial surface.
Infiltrate tissues for 8 h in freshly made propylene oxide: embedding resin mix 1:3 at RT with rotation.
Infiltrate tissues overnight in freshly made pure embedding resin at RT with rotation.
Agitate gently to prevent samples from attaching to the vial surface.
Place tissues in appropriate embedding molds with freshly prepared embedding resin.
Add printed labels in the mold for identification.
Thoroughly and slowly mix embedding resin ingredients prior to use.
Eliminate bubble formation in the embedding resin.
Remove bubbles from the embedding mold or capsules using pipette tips.
Place corpus callosum at the bottom of the flat embedding mold with the medial corpus callosum close to the cutting edge of the mold.
Place optic nerve at the bottom of the flat embedding mold with the anterior optic nerve close to the cutting edge of the mold.
Position spinal cord segment near the extremities of the embedding capsule.
Carefully adjust tissue position during resin polymerization using a tapered ultra-fine point tweezers.
Polymerize the embedding resin block in an oven at 60°C overnight.
Trim the polymerized embedding resin block to 1 mm² size using a single edge razor blade.
Expose the nerve within the trimmed block to make it visible.
Orientate the tissue blocks appropriately for sectioning, ensuring sections transect across longitudinal axonal bundles.
Cut resin blocks to 0.5 μm semithin sections in filtered distilled H2O using Leica EM UC6 ultramicrotome and diamond knife.
Collect and place the semithin sections on a slide with water droplets using an eyelash with handle brush.
Place the slide on a hotplate stirrer at approximately 70°C to evaporate the distilled H2O.
Circularly move the slide to flatten the sections.
Add drops of toluidine blue staining solution on the dried-out sections and incubate until the edges of the drops begin to dry.
Remove the slide from the hot plate, rinse under tap water, and dry them on the top of a hotplate.
Mount the slide with a coverslip using Permount mounting medium.
Visualize the sections using an Olympus BX61 upright motorized microscope combined with an oil immersion (100×) objective lens.
Take microscopic images in bright field.
Cut ultrathin sections using an ultramicrotome and diamond knife in filtered distilled H2O using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Collect the section directly on formvar carbon film coated single slot copper grid.
Check the collected section under a microscope to ensure it is in the right area.
Allow the sections to dry up on filter paper.
Insert the edge of the grid into the grid staining pad placed on parafilm.
Drop uranyl acetate solution to fully cover the grid, forming a solution dome.
Stain for 20 min away from direct light by covering the grid with a black lid.
Take the grid pad off from the plate holder ready for staining.
Centrifuge an appropriate volume of 4% aqueous uranyl acetate at 5,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Filter the centrifuged uranyl acetate with a 0.22 μm syringe before use.
Store filtered uranyl acetate at 4°C in a refrigerator in the dark.
Discard uranyl acetate solution.
Rinse staining pad briefly using distilled water.
Rinse the grid staining pad in three disposable beakers filled with distilled water.
Allow the grids to dry.
Rinse the grid thoroughly with water.
Stain with lead citrate for 1 min.
Filter lead citrate with a 0.22 μm syringe filter before use.
Quickly transfer grids during preparation.
Avoid breathing on grids.
Rinse the grid staining pad in three disposable beakers filled with distilled water.
Dry the grids out using filter paper.
Store grids in a grid storage box for EM imaging.
Place a piece of parafilm on a Petri dish.
Drop uranyl acetate solution on the parafilm.
Place the grid on the drop of uranyl acetate solution.
Incubate for 20 min away from direct light, covered with a black lid.
Remove the grid after incubation using forceps.
Dip the grid for 15s into three 50 mL Falcon tubes containing distilled H2O.
Drain off excess distilled H2O by gently touching filter paper to the edge of the grid.
Place a piece of parafilm in a new Petri dish.
Drop 0.3% lead citrate in 0.1 N sodium hydroxide on the grid.
Incubate for 1 min keeping the Petri dish covered with lid.
Rinse the grid 4 times for 15 s each using distilled water.
Drain off excess distilled H2O and place the grid on a clean filter paper to dry.
Store the grid in a grid box for EM imaging.
Mount the grid in a standard TEM holder.
Place the specimen facing down inside the specimen carrier.
Insert the holder into the TEM.
Turn the magnification down to find the stained sheets.
Scan the grid at low magnification (×1250) to get an overall image of the myelinated regions.
Label the outline of the myelinated region using the Stage2 control panel.
Randomly acquire 5–30 images per section at higher magnification.
Mark the stage position of different images using the Stage2 control panel.
Remove the grid from the TEM.
